[b]Heaven brings forth innumerable things to nurture man.[/b]

Before now, the world made little sense. What rationality could be found was guided through heaven. By what authority do we live benevolently and act righteously? Because it is the will of a cosmic force greater than ourselves. Heaven, the old sages say, is the unity of all things. Good and bad, hot and cold, dark and light, masculine and feminine, war and peace, life and death. Before these things and long after it was Heaven, and men endeavored to become one with Heaven through the Way and its principles.

But people forget heaven.

Not through moral degeneration and degradation, that is what the reactionaries would say. No, people forget heaven because we began to know better. The five elements became 118, the conceptualizations of qi were supplanted by microorganisms, and above all things was the realization that great action need not come from a lonesome, all-powerful throne.

It was a century since then that the Constitutionalist Army stormed the Heavenly Gates of the Holy City of Tianci and caused the downfall of the Qianxun monarchy. What is a hundred years ago to most men? A decade ago is a fond memory, fifty years perhaps a yearning of the good old days, but a century ago? To us mortal men, a century is history for a distant time. Who on Erene remembers a time when Qianxun did not call itself the Republic? When the great city of Taihe once called itself Tianci? Or a time when the symbol of the Min Zhu Party did not mark every single government building and office?

There are still remnants of the old ways, of course. The MZP continues to revere the Qianxun Classics and dares not to erase its overarching principles. Be good to your fellow man, be holistic to the needs of all people, be humble to the state, and be accepting of the natural course of human events. However, always be critical of the teachings of Republican Qianxun. What "goodness" they say is goodness to the party. To be "holistic" is to recognize that the MZP is supremacy itself, embedded into every aspect of Qianxun life. To be humble is to lay down one's arms in total submission to Min Zhu. To be accepting is to never again consider the agency of the self.

Before republicanism, and after tyranny, the declining Qianxun Empire was on track to adopt constitutionalism, but sinister forces from both left and right conspired to destroy it, and it was destroyed. Now, people no longer remember a time in which they were ruled over not by a general secretary, but by a Son of Heaven. People no longer remember that these halls and palaces that are now mere movie sets and tourist spots were once the property of a great and noble house.

[list]

"And in all honesty, screw them."  The Princess Imperial said, resting her cheek against her hand. "Those tourists were being ridiculous. If we lose money from this, then whatever."

"Language, Your Majesty," cautioned Chief Minister Boqin. "To return to the observance of the rites through self-control constitutes benevolence. Mouthing off the good men of our patron country for their innocent or morbid curiosity of this house is not benevolence."

"Bleh, it wasn't even that bad."

"Punching a tourist's child squarely in the face because they thought your hair looked funny? No, it was that bad."

[/list]

Boqin sighed and crossed his arms. He was only in his 40s but seemed 50, his onyx black hair of yesteryears now luminous with white streaks all over. Time had not been kind to him these past few years, not a decade ago during the ferocious assassination campaigns of the republicans, nor now as regent for the wily Princess Imperial. Still, stress never overcame the Chief Minister. He always wore his hanfu and his princely garb with delicacy, his skin hardly blemished save for the cracking of age, his voice clear and piercing in its commands even in the gentlest of octaves. 

Woeful, but expected it must be then, that Boqin must control the rampancy of his ward. Zhenjin, Princess Imperial, she was called. Though ARENA preferred calling her Emperor Anshi. Pale-faced, grey-eyed, persistently frustrated by the slightest of faults, apathetic, and above all, negligent of the Confucian rites. This was the darling star of the monarchist movement, the supposed figurehead of Qianxun constitutional monarchism. Yin and yang. Light and dark. Good and bad. The Chief Minister and his Emperor.

[list]

"Tourists are scum." Zhenjin continued, mindlessly twirling one of her straight-cut bangs before standing up. "They trample all over my palace floors and gawk at the fineries with their bloody phones and lament at how strange the world is in their bios. Then, they pay you for having gawked at your way of life."

"Yin and yang," Boqin said, his voice low. "In the many that are there simply for their own pleasure are the few that seek to better understand the culture of Qianxun before republicanism. We must never give up in our endeavor to restore Your Majesty to the Imperial Throne."

[/list]

Zhenjin turned around, her eyes narrowing into a squint.

[list]

"You're talking like restoration is an eventuality."

"People will tire of tyranny eventually, Your Majesty." Boqin retorted. "One day, the Min Zhu Party will overplay its hand. Drunk on victory, it will commit atrocities upon its people in search of greater gold. Then, we shall return."

"Not in my lifetime, let alone yours. ARENA seems to be so hell-bent on the idea that the only available alternative to communism is monarchy. But it's not. Many blood had been shed to kick my great-great-grandfather off the throne. A little bit of time isn't gonna be enough to make the Qianxun forget that Tianci is now Taihe and that it's "comrade" and not "sir"."

"Power and authority are the two main pillars of Qianxun society, Your Majesty. Our people do not know republic. That term is a Western invention, imposed upon us by colonizers and conquerors. Even without the imperial throne, Qianxun's society structured itself around a supreme executive power, the Min Zhu Party, general secretary Cui Fang. Without power and without authority, this is void. The people will come to love you in due time, Your Majesty."

"Maybe."

[/list]

Zhenjin shrugged her shoulders, then stood up from her chair and faced the Chief Minister. Her blue-green cheongsam glowed radiantly like fine jade in front of the sunlit window. Her eyes remained cast low, her mouth closed into a flat line, woefully unconvinced of Boqin's words.

It is comforting to put one's trust in an auspicious future, to be assured that with ample virtue, there shall happy escape from the injustices of the present. But time ticks on. It has been nearly a century since the overthrow of the monarchy. And, as Qianxun endeavors to install more communist governments in Sanguivallis, in Astanir, perhaps even Tartakum, the time for restoration slips further from their grasp. So then, perhaps the time for action should be soon? As the League of the Eight Trigrams would say?

[list]

"But it can't be now," Zhenjin said, shaking her head. "Qianxun will never allow it."

"And why not?"

"Lots of things, some more compelling than others..."

[/list]

The Princess Imperial left the illumination of the sunlight, a thin sweat forming beneath her brow, which she wiped off before walking towards the long line of bookshelves that covered the walls of the private study. Most encased books, as was their purpose, but many did not; instead, lined with file folders and dossiers, others just bundles of papers haphazardly stapled together, and many still traditional Qianxun scrolls rolled up and stacked upon each other like wine bottles. Zhenjin's hand, however, traveled instinctively to a lonesome folder that nestled at the top of the bookshelf closest to her desk, settling it down on the mahogany surface before opening its contents.

[list]

"What's that, Your Majesty?" The Chief Minister asked. "I don't suppose you've been housing anti-ARENA propaganda recently..."

"Funny you should ask that. This one was compiled by the Thrysmorans themselves, you know?" Zhenjin replied, her eyes darkening from their previous detached apathy as she combed through the pages of the folder, her attention fixed on the dates listed at the top of each document. Then, she stopped. The year was 1989. "Nearly two decades before I was born, there used to be a Qianxun couple who lived among the ARENA officials at San Lourenzo. In this report, the husband was identified as Mr. C.M., while the madam was Mrs. C.Y. They weren't members of the House of Shangguan. Nevertheless, they fled the country seeking a better life than under the communists."

"And they were right to do so." Chief Minister Boqin intoned, leaning over curiously to get a better look at the reports. "The communists lay waste to whatever they touched. Those who came with us eventually lived a good life."

"Not for Mr. C.M.," Zhenjin quickly riposted. "In 1989, Mr. C.Y. came into the ICU at the San Lourenzo General Hospital. Tuberculosis, from decades of work in construction. Over those years, his right lung had started to rot away, as though it were a piece of metal corroding away from a deluge of rust. The doctors recommended removing this lung to prevent it from filling up his left lung and literally drowning him in his own blood. But by then, he was too far gone for that sort of procedure, so the only option was to hook him up to a ventilator for what remained of his life. But even that was not enough. The couple told us that they could not afford a ventilator.

So what did they do? Boqin asked, listening intently.

Nothing. She bluntly responded. The Thrysmorans billed Mrs. C.Y. for her trouble, then kicked her out. ARENA provided some money for antibiotics for Mr. C.M. and some rice and biscuits for their child, but nothing more. Mrs. C.Y. stayed with the love of her life during his last week in a hospice bed. Then, he was gone, choked painfully in a sea of his own blood. After that, Mrs. C.Y. went with her child, a certain C.F., towards the port of San Lourenzo and disappeared shortly after. She indicated that there was nothing left for them in Thrysmora.

[/list]

Zhenjin then closed the folder, her gaze fixed squarely on the Chief Minister, whose countenance had contorted into a subtle gloom. 

[list]

"This document was recently declassified three years ago..." The Princess Imperial said, interrupting the brief silence. "... the couple's names were Mr. Cui Mingyuang and Mrs. Cui Yue. After her husband's death, Mrs. Cui Yue was found shipwrecked on the eastern coast of Amaralo and claimed to be an ARENA defector. This caused quite a buzz in Qianxun news back then, with the MZP eagerly granting Mrs. Cui and her child citizenship in return for all the juicy details they could give about the horrible lives the Qianxun live under capitalist rule... then, when Mrs. Cui passed away, her child became a darling of the Min Zhu Politburo..."

"... You can't mean..."

"The child's name was Cui Fang. Future general secretary Cui Fang." Zhenjin confirmed, her voice monotonous. "Why in the hell do we still speak of ARENA in a world that still vividly remembers the sins of our fathers?"

[/list]
